sections.churn_summary: Hold-buffer guards are live on all three tracks (`exit_confirm_screens`: 2, `reentry_cooldown_screens`: 1, `min_rebalance_notional_gbp`: 10.0), and the primary `ai_judgment` track shows materially lower cost drag (2.91%, £29.15 on 5 decision-review trades) than the control `rules` track (10.71%, £107.10 on 23 trades), with `beat_control`: true and `primary_excess_after_costs`: -0.0382 vs `control_excess_after_costs`: -0.1299. Churn is not uniformly improving: `rules` still logged 18 trades in the last 7d (9 buys, 7 sells, 2 trims, 7 full exits) and 2 adjacent buy/sell flips (HIK.L, AEP.L on 2026-07-25), while `rebalance_state.exit_streak` and `reentry_cooldown` are empty and `buffered_holdings` is 0 on every track—suggesting guards are armed but not yet accumulating streak/cooldown state in this snapshot. The single biggest operational learning gap is the `rules` control book: elevated cost drag triggered an applied `min_conviction` raise (0.15 → 0.2), yet adjacent flips and high 7d trade volume persist, so guard effectiveness vs conviction-floor tuning remains unvalidated.

sections.proposed_experiments:
1. [paper_churn] Raise `exit_confirm_screens` from 2→3 on the `rules` track only — measure whether `adjacent_flip_count` and `trades_last_7d` full exits fall without widening `excess_after_costs` gap vs `ai_judgment`.
2. [paper_churn] Counterfactual `min_rebalance_notional_gbp` sweep (10→15→20 GBP) on `rules` using last-7d trade log — quantify how many of the 18 trades would have been blocked and implied cost-drag reduction vs missed rebalance notional.
3. [offline_sim] Replay HIK.L and AEP.L adjacent flip windows with `reentry_cooldown_screens` at 1 vs 2 on `rules` — expected learning value: isolate whether cooldown length would have blocked the 2026-07-25 sell→buy pairs without changing primary-track config.
